links.label: rubric-v2 — why a human reference is the blocker

log.msg: **THE INTERACTION, and why: a DUEL — two shots side by side, click the better one, 59 times.** The alternatives were rejected for stated reasons. **(1) Drag one column of 18 into order** — the brief itself names it tedious and error-prone at the middle, and it is: it asks Mike to hold eighteen things in his head at once, and `ext/Draggable`'s `Sortable` would also need an `Item` tree (`item.move(parent, before)`) that buys nothing for a flat list of 18. **(2) Bucket into great/fine/weak, then order within buckets** — credible, and it still ends in three drag-sorts, i.e. the same problem three times smaller. **(3) Score each image 0–100** — this is the exact defect the program just measured: the same Opus model re-scoring the same pixels drifted −2.4 to −6.4 on every axis and REORDERED the corpus (rubric-v2, ICC 0.510). Asking Mike for absolute numbers would import that instability into the reference standard. **The duel wins on four counts.** It asks for a rank *primitive*, which is what a reference standard needs and the only thing with no scale to drift. It is the only shape where the images are BIG — two side by side is the largest a comparison can be, 1115px each at 3440. Binary insertion needs ~4 comparisons per image, so the middle never requires holding the corpus in mind. And it is resumable by construction: after every pick the sorted prefix is already a valid partial ranking. Measured cost: **59 comparisons worst case, 58 for a self-consistent judge, 46 for a perfectly consistent one.**

**What is stored is the JUDGEMENTS, not the order — `order` is derived on every read.** `ranking.json` holds `verdicts` (each `{better, worse, at}`, two hashes, consumed by the binary insertion sort) and `revisions` (the same record for a pair re-judged after the build, applied by promoting `better` above `worse`, inert if it already is). `order` and `pages` are written alongside for a human reader, but `build()` in `rank/rank.js` regenerates both — so undo is a `pop()`, a resume is a replay, and the raw pairwise data survives for anyone who later wants a different aggregation, or wants to measure Mike's own transitivity. **The replay refuses to guess:** if a verdict names a pair that is not the comparison the sort had reached, `broke` reports its index and the page renders a warning instead of a plausible-but-wrong order. Verified by corrupting verdict 5 — the duel disappears and the page says the file is inconsistent.

**THE SCREENSHOT ROUTE IS ALREADY LIVE ON :80 — the brief assumed it was not.** `GET /screenshot?path=…` answers 200 for the frozen PNGs right now, so the shared server has been restarted by someone since `shots-in-log` landed. I did not restart it and did not need to. The honest-degradation path was therefore tested by FORCING it (`route_gone()`): `.rank-absent` renders, **zero `` elements are created**, the copy names `node server.js` as the fix, and the standings and both correlation tables stay on screen because they need no images. Off localhost `LOCAL` is false and the probe never runs at all — the same shape `ext/AITask`'s `shots.js` and `feed.js` already use.

**Tier scores FROZEN into my own `tiers.json` rather than fetched live — the right call, because `ext/DesignTool` is mid-repair by another agent.** Sources and their `generated_at`, as asked: **taste** `ext/DesignTool/audit/taste.json` **2026-08-17T05:52:08.000Z**; **math** `ext/DesignTool/audit/findings.json` **2026-08-17T05:52:08.000Z** — both read at width **1280**, matching the corpus shoot; **Opus pass A** `vision-baseline/baseline.json`; **Opus pass B** `rubric-v2/pass-b.json`; **Sonnet** `rubric-v2/experiment.json`, the mean of the five axes averaged over the three completed **v1** passes, which is the configuration rubric-v2 recommended shipping (passes averaged, mean-of-axes, no rescale). All 18 rows joined for all 5 tiers with no gaps; sanity figures reproduce the sources exactly (opus_a mean 70.2 sd 7.98, taste 68.9 / 8.81, math 81.9 / 6.15). **One url needed remapping:** the shot of `/framework/ext/LayoutTool/tests/` was frozen before today's rename, so the audit join reads `/framework/ext/DesignTool/tests/` (taste 57, math 81 — identical to what vision-baseline logged for that page). `ranking.json` keeps the ORIGINAL url, because that is the page those pixels came from.

**The correlation code reproduces three independently published figures to three decimals — that is the only proof the payoff view is honest.** `spearman()` is Pearson over *average* ranks, so ties are handled properly (math emits only 10 distinct values across 18 pages, and the naive sum-of-d² formula is wrong with ties that heavy). Against `baseline.json`'s `overall` as the reference, my code computes **Opus pass B +0.507** (rubric-v2 published **+0.507**), **taste +0.266** (vision-baseline published **+0.266**), **math −0.039** (published **−0.039**), and Sonnet's 3-pass v1 mean **+0.180** (rubric-v2 measured its fresh v1 passes at +0.184 and +0.264 on mean-of-axes). Verified a second way straight through the UI: driving all 58 clicks while picking by `taste` score makes the page report **taste ρ +1.00**. The table also carries `mean`, `sd` and `range` per tier plus **a constant-72 control row** whose sd is 0.00 and whose ρ reads *no ordering to correlate* — so the tier that refuses to discriminate cannot look good here, which is the trap the brief flagged.

**Verified headless at 3440 / 1920 / 1280 / 400: zero console errors, zero failed requests, zero horizontal overflow, zero elements escaping the region — at every width.** Shot size, measured: **3440 → 1115px each, side by side, both fully above the fold** (87% of the PNG's native 1280, capped at `--shot` so it is never upscaled); **1920 → 468px each, side by side**; **1280 → 446px, stacked**; **400 → 344px, stacked**. Stacking is `flex-wrap` off one 20em basis with no breakpoint — deliberately a *small* basis, because a comparison needs both shots visible at once, and below it each shot takes the full region instead of halving it. Every shot's foot also carries a plain link to the PNG at true 1280 in a new tab, which is the answer whenever the region is too narrow to judge in. Interactions all verified through the real DOM: a click writes `ranking.json` immediately (there is no submit button anywhere), ← / → pick, `u` undoes, a standings-row click re-opens that pair as a duel and records a revision that reorders, and the completed state shows the done banner with 18 rows and 17 re-judgeable neighbours.

**One measurement Mike should see, because the fix is not mine to make (RULE#1).** This page renders inside `ext/catalog`'s region under `/framework/ai/`, and the chrome costs it real width: at 3440 the framework sidebar takes 274px and the catalog rail takes **738px**, leaving the page **2428** — which is why each shot is 1115px rather than a full 1280. At a 1280 viewport the same chrome leaves the page only **506px**, and that is what forces the pair to stack there rather than anything in my CSS. The rail width is already a token (`--rail`, default 19em, `catalog.css`) and `container()` is a documented seam a page can override to mount higher — but both change how every task page under `ai/` behaves, so neither belongs in a task-dir page. Recorded as a finding, not a change.

log.msg: **Fixed a live instance of CLAUDE.md's own layer trap, in my own file.** Something stripped the first two lines of `rank/rank.css` after I wrote it, deleting the `@layer base, theme, site, util;` restatement and leaving a bare `@layer theme {`. Nothing failed and nothing warned — which is the trap exactly: the FIRST `@layer` statement fixes the order, so had this sheet loaded first, `theme` alone would have appended `base`, `site` and `util` after it in first-seen order. Restored and re-verified. Worth knowing that a formatter can silently reintroduce this in any stylesheet.
